mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) consistently compresses equity discount rates and boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as observed in historical data across multiple economic cycles.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises by >0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales (both above their 3-month moving averages) indicates strengthening consumer demand and business investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 3-month moving average
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery phases, a rising industrial production index (INDPRO) signals expanding manufacturing output and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-recession recovery periods, INDPRO growth is not associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 1.0% signals the start of a monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is above 1.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 500.0 thousand units over three months indicates weakening residential construction and reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 500.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three months signal a strengthening labor market and rising consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls in 3 months
failure_condition: When PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls over three months, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession consumer recovery phases, a rising retail sales index (RSAFS) indicates improving consumer spending and business revenue, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-recession consumer recovery periods, RSAFS growth is not associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 5-year rolling window.
